## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the 37 documents in scope traces to a base rule, an overwrite, an extended rule sentence or a factor ladder. Additions checked and found to be equivalent derivations: window limits written as "no earlier than 30 days after the receipt date" (source: "the standard dating"); the "Points of judgement" boundary cases of the window docs (arithmetic restatements of the thresholds). No confirmation, review, notification or extra step was added. Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unsatisfied, first call …"): none. Opening world state written as a policy fact: none (worked examples are labelled hypothetical; none equals a figure of this task — grep of every GT value over docs/ found no dwelling-content hit).

Difference list:
- **K1 (KB-BIJECTION RED).** Overwrite 3 of each loan policy (`dwelling_waiting_period` "When both exceptions could apply, the one giving the earlier effective date is recorded.") has replaced_by "…the loan-transaction dating governs whenever it applies and the map-revision dating applies only to a request that neither the loan-transaction dating nor the renewal dating reaches; **a pending increase of the contents limit recorded for a loan transaction and a pending deductible decrease recorded for a loan transaction follow the rules written for them, a pending coverage increase the insured requested with no loan transaction follows the rules written for such requests,** and every other transaction keeps the base rule: When both exceptions could apply…". The KB carries it only in building_loan_increase_waiting_days_3dea5f4e, contents_loan_increase_waiting_days_4b526cce and deductible_loan_decrease_waiting_days_90f5d03d as "**Rule.** For a pending increase of the building limit recorded for a loan transaction …, the loan-transaction dating governs whenever it applies and the map-revision dating applies only to a request that neither the loan-transaction dating nor the renewal dating reaches; every other transaction keeps the rule that when both exceptions could apply, the one giving the earlier effective date is recorded." (and likewise for contents / deductible). The bold carve-out is dropped in all three, so each document now states that the other two loan-request kinds keep the earlier-date tie-break, contradicting those kinds' own documents. Symptom: for a loan request whose policy also carries a qualifying map revision and whose premium arrived before the closing, the building doc yields the earlier date (receipt + 1 day) for a contents or deductible request while that request's own doc yields the closing date. Root cause: replaced_by sentence not carried in full. Affected: the three `*_waiting_days` docs, "Rule." paragraph. Task 0's numbers are not affected (the policy has no map revision on record), which does not lift the RED.

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION RED — K1** (three `*_waiting_days` documents, "Rule." paragraph). Everything else in scope PASS. First revision; no previous round.

No action-form restatement; no resolving action or performer named beside them.
- Tool names: each task tool name occurs only in its own hub/invocation document (grep over all docs/).
- Hub "Scope" paragraphs list sibling request kinds ("follow the rules written for them") — verbatim overwrite text delimiting scope; they state no dependency or order. Not a finding.
- Contents/deductible rise tiers read whether the earlier increase "has been billed, its endorsement charge being booked on the premium account" — a factor tier on a record state, as the source ladder has it; no tool, route or order stated.
- Computation documents carry the generic assembly sentences of the source rule ("Where more than one date applies … the latest of them"; "adjustments first, then limits, then the credits booked with the remittance"). They name no factor quantity and come from the rule text (XF design); recorded as a policy-side note, not a KB verdict.
- Factor docs: none says which tier customers fall on, none names another factor or points at the computation document; window docs state the floor in figures rather than by naming the baseline.
- Titles: general subjects ("Coverage Changes of the Expiring Term and the Renewal Cap", "Renewal Remittance by the Insured Before the Term End", the billing schedules); none mirrors this task.
- No table, checklist, roadmap or example strings the endorsements and the renewal together.

**KB-EXPLICIT: PASS.**
